units.source_text: 我好恨呀，我好恨呀！”女童吟时那种扭扭捏捏的神气，竟与六条妃子无异。

en.t: How I hate you, how I hate you! As the little girl chanted these words, her coy, affected manner was exactly like that of the Rokujo consort.

units.source_text: 源氏相信之后，反而觉得讨厌，懊恼之极，但愿她不再开口。

en.t: Once Genji believed it, he instead felt repelled and deeply distressed, wishing only that she would say no more.

units.source_text: 岂知那鬼魂又说话了：“你提拔我的女儿，让她当了皇后，我在九泉之下，也很欢喜感谢。

en.t: But then the spirit spoke again: You raised my daughter up and made her empress, and even beneath the nine springs I am very glad and grateful.

units.source_text: 然而幽明异道，我对子女之事，其实不甚关心。

en.t: Yet the paths of the dead and the living are different, and in truth I am not greatly concerned with matters concerning my children.

units.source_text: 只是我自己心头之恨，犹自执着，未能忘怀。

en.t: It is only the resentment in my own heart that still clings to me and cannot be forgotten.

units.source_text: 就中更有最可痛恨之事：我在世时被人贬斥，受人蔑视，犹可忍也；

en.t: Among all these things, there is one that is most hateful: while I was alive, being denounced and despised by others could still be endured;

units.source_text: 而在我死之后，你们两人还要在喁喁私语之时对我恶口讥评，这才真可痛恨了！

en.t: but after my death, for the two of you still to speak ill of me and mock me in your intimate whispers, that is truly hateful!

units.source_text: 须知对于已死之人，总要处处原谅，听见别人说他坏话，尚且应该替他辩解，替他隐讳呢！

en.t: You should know that the dead ought always to be forgiven in every way; even when you hear others speak badly of them, you should defend them and cover their faults!

units.source_text: 我心久怀此恨，今已忍无可忍；身既成为恶鬼，只得显灵作祟。

en.t: My heart has long held this resentment, and now I can bear it no longer; since I have become an evil spirit, I can only appear and bring harm.

units.source_text: 我对此人并无深仇宿怨。

en.t: I have no deep hatred or old grudge against this woman.

units.source_text: 但因你身常有神佛大力守护，似觉离我甚远，使我无法接近，连你的声音也仅能隐约听到，所以只得向她发泄。

en.t: But because your body is always powerfully protected by gods and Buddhas, you seem very far from me, so that I cannot draw near and can only faintly hear your voice; therefore I have no choice but to vent my rage on her.

units.source_text: 罢了罢了！现在我但望你替我多做佛事，使我减轻罪孽。

en.t: Enough, enough! Now I only hope that you will perform many Buddhist rites for me, so that my sins may be lightened.

units.source_text: 你叫僧众大声祈祷、诵经，在我觉得火焰缠身，痛苦不堪。

en.t: When you have the monks pray and chant sutras in loud voices, it feels to me as though flames are wrapped around my body, and the pain is unbearable.

units.source_text: 我听不到慈悲的梵音，真正伤心啊！

en.t: I cannot hear the compassionate sacred voices; it is truly heartbreaking!

units.source_text: 我还要请你向皇后传言：在宫中服务，切不可心怀嫉妒，与人争吵。

en.t: I also ask you to pass a message to the empress: while serving in the palace, she must never harbor jealousy or quarrel with others.

units.source_text: 还必须多做功德，借以减轻当斋宫时渎神之罪，否则后悔莫及！”

en.t: She must also perform many good works, so as to lessen the sin of having offended the gods when she was the Saigu; otherwise regret will come too late!
The spirit poured out these words in an endless stream.

units.source_text: 源氏觉得和鬼魂谈话，不成体统，便使用法力，把鬼魂封闭于室内，悄悄地把病人迁往别室去了。

en.t: Genji felt that speaking with a spirit was improper, so he used his ritual power to confine the spirit in the room and quietly moved the sick woman to another chamber.
